source.title: Contrasting random and learned features in deep Bayesian linear regression
source.authors: Jacob A. Zavatone-Veth; W. Tong; Cengiz Pehlevan

record.tranche_reason: The study derives and checks learning curves for Bayesian linear random-feature models and deep neural networks. Its results refine the double-descent claim: bottlenecks produce model-wise divergence in random-feature models, but not in the networks with all layers trained.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study’s own theoretical and numerically checked generalization results. Results cited from other work, including the cited triple-descent literature, are not recorded as findings of this study.
record.test_reason: The study derives replica learning curves, checked numerically at d=100, for Bayesian deep linear random-feature (RF) and fully trained (NN) models. The curves show where sample-wise and model-wise divergences occur, which bears directly on V1, V3, V4 and V6. The setting is new (Bayesian, zero-temperature, isotropic Gaussian), so T3 fits better than T5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors add three points: NNs show no sample-wise divergence without noise; both models reduce to linear regression in the wide (kernel) limit; and training all layers gives a small advantage over random features, invisible at first-order perturbation theory.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses replica-based and replica-free analysis of Bayesian deep linear regression with isotropic Gaussian data, rather than the original sources’ settings and measurements. It studies asymptotic generalization error in LR, random-feature, and fully trainable linear-network models.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome depends on label noise, whether hidden layers are fixed random features or trainable NN layers, and whether the narrowest layer is below the input dimension. In RF models, the narrowest bottleneck determines the visible divergence; adding label noise does not add an α=1 divergence when γmin<1.

fits_no_version.finding: RF models have an interior optimal width and optimal depth when the prior variance exceeds the target scale (σ̃>1). For NNs, the optimum is always infinite or vanishing width.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prior–target scale mismatch determines whether wider or deeper Bayesian linear models generalize better.

record.problems: The replica-symmetry calculation is non-rigorous, and the paper notes possible replica-symmetry breaking in deep linear NNs. Its conclusions concern a specialized Bayesian linear model with isotropic Gaussian covariates and zero-temperature likelihood; numerical simulations use d=100. The reported plots include ±2 SE bars, but the principal claims are largely stated through analytic asymptotic curves.

untested.parts: No training-time or epoch axis; the analysis is of Bayesian posteriors.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested across axes. The RF peak sits at γmin=α on both axes, but the authors do not frame this as a complexity measure.
Whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak is not tested; the prior variance σ is varied but not optimized against the divergence.
Nonlinear networks and gradient-trained networks are not studied; only Bayesian deep linear models are.

missing.what: RF width sweep at α>1 (Fig. 2b,d): error decreases monotonically with γmin, with no model-wise peak, and is zero for γmin>1 without noise.
missing.locator: Section IV A, Fig. 2(b,d); Appendix F1 last paragraph

missing.what: RF error rises monotonically in γmin over [0,α) when α<1 before the divergence. This is the shape of the approach to the peak: no initial fall.

record.verdict_notes: Results rest on a non-rigorous replica-symmetric ansatz, which may break for NNs, checked numerically at d=100. Divergences are infinite in the thermodynamic limit. The Bayesian zero-temperature posterior, not SGD training, limits how far the findings transfer to the original deep-network claims.

versions.untested_parts: Tests width variation in the studied Bayesian linear architectures, not model-size sweeps in nonlinear or conventionally trained deep networks.
No sweep over training epochs or training time.
Tests sample density in the studied high-dimensional Gaussian regression setting, not general datasets or training procedures.
Tests linear regression, random-feature models, and deep linear Bayesian networks; does not cover other model classes.
Does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak location across size, epochs, and samples.
Tests label-noise and bottleneck effects, but not variance as a distinct mechanism or whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak.
Does not re-count complexity using an effective number of parameters or test whether that turns the second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

conditions.value: η=0 for the stated absence of model-wise divergence
σ=1 in the stated width-invariance example

rows.measure: Generalization error ε as a function of hidden-layer width
rows.value: Bottlenecks do not induce model-wise double descent or a model-wise divergence in NN models; for σ=1 and η=0, the error is constant as widths vary
rows.note: The paper also reports that width has relatively minimal effect at non-zero noise when σ=1.
rows.check: The V6 link is dropped. Context matters here: a scalar-output linear NN can represent any end-to-end w at any width, so width never crosses an interpolation threshold. The authors' explanation is that a solution with one nonzero weight per layer reduces the NN to LR.

source_check.correct: The reported flat width dependence at σ=1 and η=0 is correct. For V1 and V4, use cannot_determine: this scalar-output NN width sweep crosses no interpolation threshold.
source_check.locator_found: Section V A, expressivity explanation and σ=1, η=0 identity; Fig. 5.
source_check.problem: The raw absence of a width peak does not test interpolation-transition behavior when no width transition exists.

tranche.reason: The study derives and numerically checks double-descent behavior in a new setting: deep Bayesian linear regression with random versus learned features.

source_check.notes: Errors are thermodynamic-limit Gibbs-estimator risks, including posterior variance; replica-symmetric predictions are checked against alternative calculations and d=100 simulations. Optimally tuned regularization is not tested.

statements.correction: Noiseless LR: monotone decrease to zero as α↑1, then zero. Noiseless NN: no sample-wise divergence. At σ=1 and η=0: NN equals LR. Noiseless bottlenecked RF: divergence at α→γmin.
statements.problem: For this study, the general noiseless NN result rules out sample-wise divergence; it does not establish the statement's broader absence of any harmful sample increase.

statements.correction: Scalar-output fully trained linear NN: no width interpolation transition. At σ=1 and η=0: error is independent of hidden-layer widths. V4 verdict for this condition: none.
statements.problem: The study-specific facts are correct, but the challenges label is unsupported: its fully trained NN width sweep has no interpolation transition.
